name: What happens to the surrounding walls and floor when a tub is removed?

mainEntity.name: What happens to the surrounding walls and floor when a tub is removed?

acceptedAnswer.text: Demolition is only the first phase; tub removal directly impacts the surrounding walls, subfloor, and plumbing rough-ins. When a tub is pulled, adjacent drywall and wall tile must usually be cut back to expose the framing and plumbing valves. If you plan to leave the space as an open floor or install a barrier-free shower, the contractor will need to patch drywall, address any subfloor moisture issues, and prep surfaces for new tile or flooring. Abraham Becerra coordinates needed plumbing sub-trades while his finish carpentry and drywall crew handles the wall reconstruction.
acceptedAnswer.description: Surrounding drywall, tile, and subfloor are exposed and often modified. Contractors must address plumbing valves, repair subfloors, and prep wall framing for new finishes.
